about: Wrong answers that point to a specific misunderstanding about decimals. 'pointsTo' is the subskill to work on. Claude's draft (2026-11-20), waiting for owner review.

misconceptions.description: Puts digits in the wrong place: 7/100 written 0.7, 25/1000 as 0.25, 0.4 = 4/100, or reads the wrong place.
Thinks a decimal with more digits is bigger (0.45 > 0.5, because 45 > 5).
Thinks a decimal with fewer digits is bigger, because tenths are bigger pieces than hundredths (0.4 > 0.45).
Cuts the digits off instead of rounding (2.67 to the nearest tenth = 2.6).
Rounds the wrong way (2.22 to the nearest tenth = 2.3).
Rounds to a different place than asked.
Writes the fraction's numbers as the decimal (3/4 = 0.34 or 3.4).
Divides the bottom by the top (4/5 = 1.25).
Puts the decimal's digits over 10 whatever the place (0.35 = 35/10).
Lines up the last digits instead of the decimal points (3.5 + 1.25 = 1.60; 3.25 + 2 = 3.27).
With a whole number, subtracts only the whole parts and brings the decimal part down (6 − 2.35 = 4.35).
Moves the decimal point the wrong way, or not far enough, for 10, 100, 1000 (4.5 × 10 = 0.45).
Multiplies by 10 by writing a 0 on the end, which doesn't change a decimal (2.5 × 10 = 2.50).
Places the point from one factor instead of counting the places in both (0.3 × 0.2 = 0.6).
Divides the digits right but puts the point in the wrong place (4.8 ÷ 6 = 8).
Moves the point in only one of the numbers when dividing by a decimal (2.4 ÷ 0.3 = 0.8).
Thinks a repeating decimal equals a cut-off or rounded one (2/3 = 0.6 or 0.67).
Decides whether a decimal ends by the denominator being odd or even (thinks 7/12 ends, 3/15 repeats), instead of checking for only 2s and 5s after simplifying.
Writes a repeating decimal as if it ended (0.555… = 5/10, 0.2727… = 27/100).
Adds or subtracts the decimals right but gets the sign wrong (−3.5 + 1.2 = 2.3).
Ignores the second number's sign when subtracting (3.25 − (−1.4) worked as 3.25 − 1.4).
Multiplies or divides right but gets the sign wrong (−0.3 × (−0.2) = −0.06).
